gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the three 10,000 mAh banks it recommended all collapse to 15–22.5 W total the moment a second device is plugged in, and that Anker's own support page puts the label 'rated capacity' of a 10,000 mAh pack at about 6,068 mAh at 5 V (10 Ah × 3.7 V = 37 Wh ÷ 5 V × 82 %).
standout_why: Compared against Engadget (Feb 2026: measured ~5,800 mAh of phone charge per 10,000 mAh, '~60 percent' average, no per-product rated figures and no multi-port caps), knowledgelib.io (Nov 2026: generic unsourced '65-70%' effective capacity, no per-product figure, no multi-port caps), and Anker's own best-power-bank blog (Apr 2026: no rated capacity, no Wh for the 10K picks, no combined-output caps). TechRadar's page would not render and WSJ is paywalled. None of the readable rivals shows the maker-stated label capacity (Anker A1388: 6,200 mAh at 5 V; Anker formula: 6,068 mAh), the maker's own usable-capacity estimate for the Baseus AM52 (5,500–6,500 mAh), or the fact that the 45 W Anker Nano drops to 22.5 W total (15 W cable + 7.5 W port) with two devices and the 22.5 W Anker A1388 drops to 15 W total. Engadget's measured 58 % is the closest and is a real measurement, so this is new-and-useful rather than pick-deciding.
decides: Confirms ChatGPT's '1.5–2 charges' row but tightens it: by the makers' own numbers a 10,000 mAh phone bank holds about 6,000–6,200 mAh at 5 V, so it is roughly 1.2–1.3 fills of a 5,000 mAh Android flagship or ~1.7 fills of an iPhone 17 (~3,600 mAh class), not 2. It also shifts the pick between ChatGPT's 'everyday' and 'premium' choices: the $59.99 Anker Nano 45W's headline wattage only applies to one device at a time (45 W Samsung, 40 W iPhone 17); charge a phone and earbuds together and it is a 22.5 W bank, the same total as the $25.88 Anker A1388 charging one device. For a single phone the 45 W is real; for two devices the extra $34 buys the retractable cable, not speed. Baseus PicoGo AM52 ($55.99, Dealectric-listed) is the only candidate whose maker publishes a usable-capacity estimate on the product page, and it adds Qi2.2 25 W wireless the ChatGPT picks lack.

findings.label: Maker formula: label 'rated capacity' of a 10,000 mAh bank at 5 V
findings.source_title: Why Is the Rated Capacity Marked on a Power Bank Lower Than Expected? – Anker Support
findings.note: Anker's own worked example: cells 'typically operate at a voltage of around 3.7V'; '10Ah × 3.7V = 37Wh'; rated output 'calculated at a standard output voltage of 5V' → 7,400 mAh; 'typically around 82% efficiency'; 'Rated Capacity = 7,400mAh × 0.82 = 6,068mAh'; 'a 10,000mAh power bank might typically display a rated capacity around 6,000mAh on its label.' Page undated.

findings.label: Label rated capacity at 5 V vs cell capacity
findings.source_title: Anker Power Bank PowerCore 10000mAh 22.5W A1388H11 – Pixelzones
findings.note: Retailer spec sheet quoting the label: 'Cell Capacity: 10,000mAh (3.7V / 37Wh)', 'Rated Capacity: 6200mAh (5V)'. Anker's US product page for A1388 returned 404 and Anker's service page (https://service.anker.com/product-description/a08J1000000YcHgIAK, read 2026-11-08) lists ports and protocol tables but no Wh or rated capacity, so this is a retailer-transcribed label, one tier below maker. Consistent with Anker's own 6,068 mAh formula above.

findings.label: Total output with two devices
findings.source_title: Anker Power Bank PowerCore 10000mAh 22.5W A1388H11 – Pixelzones
findings.note: 'Total Output: 5V 3A (15W max)'. Single-port 22.5 W is the Huawei SCP 10 V 2.25 A step; Anker's service page lists PD as 9 V 2.22 A (20 W) only, so a non-Huawei phone gets 20 W from one port and 15 W shared across two. Anker service page: https://service.anker.com/product-description/a08J1000000YcHgIAK (read 2026-11-08).

findings.label: Single-device vs multi-device output
findings.value: 45 W (Samsung) / 40 W (iPhone 17) one device; 22.5 W total for two or three devices
findings.source_title: Anker Nano Power Bank (10K, 45W, Built-In Retractable USB-C Cable) – Anker US
findings.note: Specs: USB-C cable/port '5V⎓3A / 9V⎓3A / 10V⎓2.25A / 15V⎓3A/ 20V⎓2.25A (45W Max)'; USB-A '22.5W Max'; 'Combined USB-C Port and USB-C Cable: 22.5W Max (15W for USB-C Cable, 7.5W for USB-C Port)'; 'Combined USB-C Port, USB-C Cable and USB-A Port: 22.5W Max (7.5W for Each)'; 'Only the USB-C port / cable supports 45W max output for Samsung and 40W max output for iPhone 17 series.' Input 30 W max. Weight 0.51 lb. Price $59.99 on 2026-11-08. No Wh or 5 V rated capacity stated on the US or UK (https://www.anker.com/uk/products/a1638) page; the A1638 user-guide PDF could not be text-extracted in this sandbox.

findings.label: Reviewer-measured phone fills
findings.value: iPhone 15 to 52 % in 30 min; 'sufficient to fully charge an iPhone 15 twice'; recharge ≈2 h 15 min at 30 W
findings.source_title: Anker Nano 10K Power Bank 45W review – Macworld (Thomas Bergbold, 23 Oct 2025)
findings.note: Thomas Bergbold's test figures; no Wh or mAh delivered was measured. iPhone 15 battery ≈3,350 mAh, so two fills ≈6,700 mAh delivered, in line with the ~6,000–6,200 mAh label range above.

findings.value: about 5,500–6,500 mAh usable (35–45 % losses) from 10,000 mAh

No Wh, no 5 V rated capacity, no per-port or total-output table. US Black $24.99, TropicPunch/SunsetBurst $22.99 (compare-at $30.99). findings.label: Rival measured delivery for comparison
findings.source_title: The best power banks and portable chargers for every device in 2026 – Engadget (Amy Skorheim, 13 Feb 2026)
findings.note: 'In our tests, 10,000mAh of battery pack capacity translated to roughly 5,800mAh of device charge'; 'average efficiency rate of around 60 percent'. Engadget's number is a measurement across its picks, not of the three ChatGPT cards; Anker's label formula (6,068 mAh) and the A1388 label (6,200 mAh) sit just above it, which is expected because label rating excludes phone-side losses.

unsourced: Anker A1638 Nano 45W: Wh and 5 V rated capacity. Looked on the Anker US page, Anker UK page, Anker service page, and the A1638 user-guide PDF (PDF downloaded but text extraction was blocked in this sandbox; retailer pages list 36.3 Wh but no maker page confirms it).

Anker A1388: a maker-hosted statement of the 6,200 mAh / 37 Wh label figures. Anker US product URL is 404; the service page lists protocol tables only; the quick-start PDF could not be extracted. The figure above comes from a retailer's transcription of the label.
